section_summary: This section concerns applications, clearances, military permits, and related diplomatic correspondence for businessmen, missionaries, dependents, and other foreign travelers seeking to enter or transit occupied Japan in 1947. It documents SCAP entry approvals, national trade quotas, missionary travel, exit-permit questions, security file checks, and attempts to change entry dates or correct permits. Major cases include William Zamara, Cherif Soubra, Teofilo Homsany Missri, Lucien Joseph Elmaleh, Meyer Abadi, several Catholic missionaries, and Japanese repatriates wishing to ship goods.

subfiles.title: Commerce application for proposed business visit to Japan, continuation
subfiles.about: Proposed commercial visit to Osaka and Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: The applicant lists Japanese contacts and proposes renewing trade in manufactured goods and cotton.

subfiles.title: Correction of Nourafehan's name on military permit
subfiles.about: Correction of a misspelled permit holder's name.
subfiles.summary: Captain Keough authorized correcting Elias Nourafehan's misspelled name in ink.

subfiles.title: Notification of William Zamara's entry clearance
subfiles.about: Arrangements to notify Zamara in Bangkok of his Japanese clearance.
subfiles.summary: The Czech Embassy authorized a charged cable to Bangkok because it maintained no mission there.

subfiles.title: Security file check on William Zamara and Kotva Inc.
subfiles.about: Search for adverse information on Zamara, Kotva, and associated Japanese firms.
subfiles.summary: Departmental searches found no records on Zamara or Kotva and only an old report concerning Okura & Co.

subfiles.title: Czechoslovak note transmitting William Zamara's application
subfiles.about: Formal transmission of Zamara's Japanese entry application.
subfiles.summary: The Czechoslovak Embassy asks the State Department to forward Zamara's application to the appropriate military authorities.

subfiles.title: William Zamara application for permission to enter Japan
subfiles.from: William Zamara via the Czechoslovak Embassy
subfiles.about: Business-entry application by Kotva Inc.'s Far East agent.
subfiles.summary: Zamara seeks six to twelve months in Tokyo to restore Kotva's prewar business and establish new contacts. He would travel from Bangkok by ship or plane and lists several former Japanese trading partners.

subfiles.title: Military permit for William Zamara
subfiles.about: Permit for entry to Japan under the traders' quota.
subfiles.summary: Zamara is authorized one journey from Bangkok and a 21-day stay under the Japan traders' quota.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Zamara application
subfiles.about: Acknowledgment and explanation of quota review.
subfiles.summary: State forwards Zamara's application for consideration under the Inter-Allied Trade Board quota for other nations.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Zamara application to War Department
subfiles.about: Request to place Zamara's application before SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Chappell asks that Zamara be considered under the trade quota assigned to other nations.

subfiles.title: Clearance notice for Cristina Estrada and Monserrat Barjau
subfiles.about: Theater clearance for two nuns to travel to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The War Department reports clearance and awaits applications before issuing military permits.

subfiles.title: Duplicate clearance notice for Cristina Estrada and Monserrat Barjau
subfiles.about: Duplicate notice of Japanese theater clearance.
subfiles.summary: Lynch confirms clearance for the two nuns on commercial or space-available revenue transportation.

subfiles.title: Confusion over Estrada, Barjau, and Martindale travel
subfiles.about: Clarification of mistaken missionary names and suspension of action.
subfiles.summary: Mohler reported that Barjau was unknown and Martindale was intended instead; later neither Estrada nor Martindale would go.

subfiles.title: Military permit sent for Elias Nourafehan
subfiles.about: Delivery of Nourafehan's Japanese military permit.
subfiles.summary: Chappell sends Nourafehan's 21-day permit, explains photographs, and confirms waiver of the United States exit permit.

subfiles.title: Czechoslovak note confirming Zamara's clearance
subfiles.about: Formal notice of Zamara's approved entry window.
subfiles.summary: State confirms Zamara may enter Japan between November 16 and 30 for three weeks. Because Czechoslovakia has no Bangkok post, clearance information will be cabled to the American representative there.

subfiles.title: Lebanese request for Cherif Soubra's visa
subfiles.about: Renewed request for Soubra to study Japanese trade opportunities.
subfiles.summary: Lebanon asks for an immediate visa for Cherif Soubra, appointed by its Ministry of National Economy to investigate trade with Japan.

subfiles.title: Clearance for Carlos Hounie Fleurquin
subfiles.about: Military clearance for Uruguay's trade representative.
subfiles.summary: Fleurquin may enter Japan with initial occupation-force support; his wife's application may be reconsidered after independent arrangements.

subfiles.title: Memorandum to Uruguay concerning Fleurquin's clearance
subfiles.about: Terms of Fleurquin's clearance and conditions for his wife's later application.
subfiles.summary: State relays the military clearance, assumes Fleurquin will perform no diplomatic or consular functions, and explains that Mrs. Fleurquin can be reconsidered once he obtains independent facilities.

subfiles.title: Review of Cherif Soubra's renewed application
subfiles.about: Procedural review of Lebanon's renewed request for Soubra.
subfiles.summary: Officials confirm Soubra's identity, review his earlier rejection, and decide to resubmit him as a private businessman under Lebanon's quota.

subfiles.title: Renewed request for Soubra's admission
subfiles.about: Request that SCAP reconsider Soubra under the other-nations quota.
subfiles.summary: Chappell asks the Military Permit Section to submit Soubra's renewed trade-study request to SCAP.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Lebanon's renewed Soubra request
subfiles.about: Notification that Soubra's case was sent to military authorities.
subfiles.summary: State says Soubra's application will be considered under national business quotas and promises notice of the decision.

subfiles.title: Stamped copy of Missri military-clearance memorandum
subfiles.about: Entry clearance and conditions for Teofilo Homsany Missri.
subfiles.summary: Missri receives a September entry window, three-week stay, Osaka lodging, and instructions for requesting an extension.

subfiles.title: Missri military-clearance memorandum
subfiles.about: Clean copy of Missri's clearance conditions.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum limits Missri to three weeks and explains lodging, photographs, and the procedure for extending his stay.

subfiles.title: Request to change Missri's entry dates
subfiles.about: Panama seeks an October entry window for Missri.
subfiles.summary: Because Missri could not arrive by September 16, officials asked SCAP to substitute an October 1–15 entry period.

subfiles.title: Letter requesting amendment of Missri's entry dates
subfiles.about: Return of Missri's permit for possible date amendment.
subfiles.summary: Chappell returns the permit and requests an October entry window, with notice for the Panamanian Embassy.

subfiles.title: Memorandum to Panama on Missri's clearance
subfiles.about: Status and conditions of Missri's Japanese entry clearance.
subfiles.summary: State explains the original clearance and its effort to obtain October dates. It also details the three-week limit, extension procedure, Japanese-operated lodging in Osaka, and photograph requirement.

subfiles.title: Swift request for W. K. Clark's military permit
subfiles.from: W. K. Clark, Swift International Company
subfiles.about: Request for a Japanese permit before Clark's planned Manila departure.
subfiles.summary: Swift supplies Clark's Canadian passport details and asks that authorization be sent to Manila if not issued before departure.

subfiles.title: Helpers of the Holy Souls request for expedited departure permits
subfiles.from: Mother Mary of St. Cecilia, Helpers of the Holy Souls
subfiles.about: Urgent request for two nuns' departure-permit applications.
subfiles.summary: The order asks prompt action so two missionaries can sail for Japan before September ends.

subfiles.title: Alien departure application of Marie Anne Le Bouteiller
subfiles.about: Departure application for a French missionary visiting Japan and returning to Shanghai.
subfiles.summary: Le Bouteiller, known as Marie de St. Joachim, seeks to sail from San Francisco to visit mission houses in Hiroshima and Yawata before returning home near Shanghai. The form supplies her identity, travel, religious affiliation, and financial information.

subfiles.title: Dreyfus acknowledgment concerning Lucien Elmaleh
subfiles.about: Company awaits Elmaleh's reply from Shanghai.
subfiles.summary: Dreyfus reports that it cabled Shipley's letter to Elmaleh and will respond after hearing from him.

subfiles.title: Draft notification of Elmaleh's entry clearance
subfiles.about: Elmaleh's September entry clearance and substitute passport endorsement.
subfiles.summary: The draft announces Elmaleh's 21-day clearance and directs notification of him and the French representative in Shanghai.

subfiles.title: Lucien Elmaleh application to visit Japan
subfiles.from: Lucien Joseph Elmaleh and Louis Dreyfus & Co.
subfiles.about: Business application to investigate Japanese commodity trade and establish a branch.
subfiles.summary: Elmaleh proposes visiting Tokyo, Osaka, and Kobe to study commodity shipments and reopening company operations. The application describes the firm's capitalization, goods, prewar trade, and former Japanese offices.

subfiles.title: Corporate background supporting Elmaleh's application
subfiles.about: Ownership and management information for Elmaleh's employer.
subfiles.summary: The company describes Leval & Co.'s officers, ownership, Far Eastern branches, and plan for a Tokyo branch.

subfiles.title: Internal forwarding note concerning George Black's letter
subfiles.about: Transfer of an enclosed letter to the appropriate office.
subfiles.summary: The sender forwards a letter that apparently does not belong in the originating division.

subfiles.title: George Black inquiry about repatriates' merchandise
subfiles.about: Permits for Oishi and Fukusaka to ship merchandise to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Black requests action on sizable merchandise shipments for two Japanese nationals being repatriated from Canada.

subfiles.title: Reply to Black on shipping goods to Japan
subfiles.about: Procedures governing commercial merchandise and personal effects.
subfiles.summary: Chappell directs commercial import requests to SCAP's Foreign Trade Division and explains that repatriates may carry reasonable personal and family effects under applicable regulations.

subfiles.title: Instruction to Vancouver consular officer to forward Black letter
subfiles.to: American Consular Officer in Charge, Vancouver
subfiles.about: Forwarding the Department's response to George Black.
subfiles.summary: The Vancouver consular office is asked to deliver the enclosed reply concerning Oishi and Fukusaka.

subfiles.title: Duplicate instruction to Vancouver consular officer
subfiles.to: American Consular Officer in Charge, Vancouver
subfiles.about: Duplicate forwarding instruction in the Black case.
subfiles.summary: A duplicate directs delivery of the Department's letter to George W. Black.

subfiles.title: Rome airgram requesting SCAP Circular No. 8
subfiles.about: Missing instructions for endorsing Assunta Prestofilippo's passport.
subfiles.summary: The embassy cannot execute Washington's instructions because neither it nor local Army headquarters has SCAP Circular No. 8.

subfiles.title: Instructions to Rome concerning Assunta Prestofilippo
subfiles.about: Entry clearance and documentation for an Italian missionary.
subfiles.summary: State reports Prestofilippo's clearance and instructs Rome to arrange a passport statement serving in lieu of a military permit.

subfiles.title: File check on Assunta Prestofilippo
subfiles.about: Departmental search for records on Prestofilippo.
subfiles.summary: Searches of several Department divisions found no correspondence concerning Sister Assunta R. Prestofilippo.

subfiles.title: Conversation about clearance of seven missionaries
subfiles.about: War Department confirmation of a telegram approving seven missionaries.
subfiles.summary: Mrs. Flickinger confirmed the clearances had no expiration and allowed State to notify interested parties before the formal memorandum arrived.

subfiles.title: CINCFE message approving seven missionaries
subfiles.about: Entry approval and transportation for seven named missionaries.
subfiles.summary: Tokyo recommends permits and space-available revenue transportation for seven missionaries, with later instructions on household goods and food.

subfiles.title: Theater clearance for Bellefonis, Suryot, and Kruse
subfiles.about: Japanese travel clearance for three religious workers.
subfiles.summary: The War Department reports theater clearance and requests applications before issuing military permits.

subfiles.title: Reply to Rome enclosing travel instructions
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge, American Mission, Rome
subfiles.about: Response to Rome's request for missing SCAP instructions.
subfiles.summary: State encloses Foreign Service serials 667 and 668 concerning Prestofilippo's documentation.

subfiles.title: Telegram to Shanghai concerning Elmaleh
subfiles.about: Notification and passport documentation for Elmaleh's Japanese entry.
subfiles.summary: The consul must notify Elmaleh and the French representative of his clearance and required English passport statement.

subfiles.title: Routing memorandum on Elmaleh case
subfiles.about: Transfer of Elmaleh correspondence and permit documents.
subfiles.summary: Shipley forwards case papers; a later note says Shanghai had already endorsed Elmaleh's passport.

subfiles.title: Military permit for Lucien Joseph Elmaleh
subfiles.about: Permit under the Japan traders' quota.
subfiles.summary: Elmaleh receives a one-journey permit allowing a 21-day stay and requiring two standard passport photographs.

subfiles.title: Dreyfus request to cable Elmaleh's clearance
subfiles.about: Request for immediate notification of the Shanghai consulate.
subfiles.summary: Dreyfus asks State to cable Elmaleh's clearance and explains his French citizenship, passport, and corporate affiliations.

subfiles.title: Processing of British applicants through British authorities
subfiles.about: Jurisdiction over three British applications for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Lynch states that British nationals must be processed through their own military authorities under SCAP Circular No. 8.

subfiles.title: Resolution of Jean Ashman's exit-permit case
subfiles.about: Investigation of the Ashmans' departure for Bombay.
subfiles.summary: Officials confirm the Ashmans sailed without needing a Japanese transit permit and arrange follow-up on Jean Ashman's United States reentry permit.

subfiles.title: War Department letter concerning Maria Dajkovich
subfiles.about: Copies of earlier memoranda on Dajkovich's permanent relocation.
subfiles.summary: Lynch sends two prior memoranda and states future cases will go to Protective Services instead of the Visa Division.

subfiles.title: Original clearance memorandum for Maria Dajkovich
subfiles.about: Approval for Dajkovich to join her daughter permanently in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Dajkovich is accepted for permanent residence because she is destitute and dependent on her daughter.

subfiles.title: Follow-up on notification of Maria Dajkovich
subfiles.about: Tokyo reports Dajkovich has not received notice of her clearance.
subfiles.summary: Keough asks that Hungarian authorities be contacted to facilitate Dajkovich's journey.

subfiles.title: NCWC transmittal of Lucie de Nervo's departure application
subfiles.about: Submission of a missionary's exit-permit application.
subfiles.summary: Mohler forwards Lucie de Nervo's application for travel to mission houses in Tokyo, Hiroshima, and Yawata.

subfiles.title: Helpers of the Holy Souls support letter for Lucie de Nervo
subfiles.about: Purpose and financial support for de Nervo's Asian mission visit.
subfiles.summary: The order explains de Nervo's planned visits with Mother St. Radegonde and assumes responsibility for both travelers.

subfiles.title: Alien departure application of Lucie de Nervo
subfiles.about: Application for departure to Japan, China, and France.
subfiles.summary: De Nervo, known as Marie de Ste. Cesarine, proposes visiting mission houses in Tokyo, Hiroshima, Yawata, and Shanghai before returning to Paris. The application records her identity, passport, religious work, finances, references, and intended September sailing.

subfiles.title: Security file check on Meyer Abadi
subfiles.about: Search for adverse records concerning Abadi.
subfiles.summary: Searches found only earlier visas and a Panama report about an aviation school, with no indication of subversive activity.

subfiles.title: English translation of Panama's note transmitting Abadi's application
subfiles.about: Panama submits Abadi's application for travel to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Chevalier forwards two application copies and requests notification of the decision.

subfiles.title: Spanish original of Panama's Abadi note
subfiles.about: Original Spanish transmittal of Abadi's application.
subfiles.summary: Panama formally sends Abadi's request and asks to be informed of its disposition.

subfiles.title: Meyer Abadi application for permission to enter Japan
subfiles.about: Panamanian merchant's request to resume pending business in Kobe.
subfiles.summary: Abadi seeks a six-month stay in Kobe to handle export business left pending when he departed Japan in September 1941. He plans to travel from Panama by ship or plane.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Meyer Abadi's application to War Department
subfiles.about: Request that SCAP consider Abadi under the other-nations quota.
subfiles.summary: Chappell forwards Abadi's application for consideration under the Inter-Allied Trade Board quota.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Panama's Abadi submission
subfiles.from: Norman Armour for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Notice that Abadi's application was sent to military authorities.
subfiles.summary: State confirms quota-based review and promises to inform Panama when a decision is received.

subfiles.title: Airgram announcing James Doyle's clearance
subfiles.about: Documentation of Doyle's missionary entry to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Dublin is told to arrange an English passport statement serving instead of a military permit and to notify Irish authorities.

subfiles.title: Name check on Reverend James Doyle
subfiles.about: Departmental search for records concerning Doyle.
subfiles.summary: Searches across several Department files revealed no information concerning Reverend James Doyle.

subfiles.title: Irish Legation note submitting applications for O'Brien and Doyle
subfiles.about: Request for Japanese entry permission for two Maynooth missionaries.
subfiles.summary: The Irish Legation encloses triplicate applications for Joseph Francis O'Brien and James Doyle and requests permission for both.

subfiles.title: James Doyle application for permission to enter Japan
subfiles.from: James Doyle via the Irish Legation
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Joint Chiefs of Staff
subfiles.about: Irish clergyman's application for indefinite missionary service in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Doyle seeks entry from Ireland via the United States to perform missionary work in Tokyo for an indefinite period.
